plan: [ This is strategically equivalent to a second-price auction: the winner pays the second-highest sealed bid. In such auctions with independent private values, the dominant strategy to maximize expected profit is to bid your true value. Overbidding risks paying more than the item is worth; underbidding risks losing when winning would be profitable. There’s no benefit to strategic shading here, and there’s only one round, so no learning/exploration value. I will bid exactly my value: 26. ]

[ This is strategically equivalent to a sealed-bid second-price auction because the winner pays the second-highest sealed bid. With independent private values, bidding your true value is a weakly dominant strategy: overbidding risks paying more than your value; underbidding risks losing profitable wins. There is no prior history to exploit and only one round, so maximize expected profit by setting the exit price equal to my value. My value is 18, so I bid 18. ]

[ This mechanism is strategically equivalent to a second-price (Vickrey) auction: the highest sealed bid wins and pays the second-highest bid (the exit price of the second-to-last bidder). With independent private values and risk-neutral preferences, the weakly dominant strategy is to bid your true value. Overbidding risks negative payoff if you win at a price above value; underbidding risks losing when winning would have been profitable. There is only 1 round, so no reputational or dynamic considerations. Therefore, bid exactly my value: 21. ]
